problems.text: If it is raining, then the streets are wet. It is raining. What can you conclude?

problems.text: Sam is in either New York or London. Sam is not in New York. What can you conclude?
Either the server crashed or the network is down. The server did not crash. What follows?
Either math or science is scheduled for Monday. Math is not scheduled for Monday. What can you conclude?

Either Riley drives or takes the subway. Riley does not drive. What can you conclude?
Either the test passed or there is a bug. The test passed. What can you conclude about whether there is a bug?
problems.ground_truth: We cannot conclude anything additional from this alone.

problems.text: Either the movie starts at 7 or at 9. It does not start at 7. What follows?
Either we go hiking or swimming. We do not go hiking. What can you conclude?

Either the cat is inside or outside. The cat is not inside. What can you conclude?
Either Python or Java was used. Python was not used. What follows?

Either the flight is on time or delayed. The flight is not on time. What follows?

Either renewable or fossil fuel powers this city. Fossil fuel does not power it. What follows?
Either Quinn or Piper won the prize. Quinn did not win. What can you conclude?
'If it is a dog, it is an animal.' What is the contrapositive of this statement?
problems.ground_truth: If it is not an animal, then it is not a dog.

problems.text: 'If it rains, the picnic is cancelled.' What is the contrapositive?
problems.ground_truth: If the picnic is not cancelled, then it is not raining.

problems.text: 'If you are a citizen, you can vote.' State the contrapositive.
problems.ground_truth: If you cannot vote, then you are not a citizen.

problems.text: 'If the shape is a square, it has four equal sides.' What is the contrapositive?
problems.ground_truth: If it does not have four equal sides, then it is not a square.

problems.text: 'If the battery is dead, the car won't start.' State the contrapositive.
problems.ground_truth: If the car starts, then the battery is not dead.

problems.text: 'If Alice passed, she studied.' What is the contrapositive?
problems.ground_truth: If Alice did not study, then she did not pass.

problems.text: 'If a number is even, it is divisible by 2.' What is the contrapositive?
problems.ground_truth: If a number is not divisible by 2, then it is not even.

problems.text: 'If the light is green, you may proceed.' State the contrapositive.
problems.ground_truth: If you may not proceed, then the light is not green.

problems.text: 'If there is smoke, there is fire.' What is the contrapositive?
problems.ground_truth: If there is no fire, then there is no smoke.

problems.text: 'If it is winter, it is cold.' State the contrapositive.
problems.ground_truth: If it is not cold, then it is not winter.

problems.text: 'If you eat too much sugar, you gain weight.' What is the contrapositive?
problems.ground_truth: If you do not gain weight, then you did not eat too much sugar.

problems.text: 'If the homework is done, the student may play.' State the contrapositive.
problems.ground_truth: If the student may not play, then the homework is not done.

problems.text: 'If X > 10, then X > 5.' What is the contrapositive?
problems.ground_truth: If X is not greater than 5, then X is not greater than 10.

problems.text: 'If Leo is a doctor, Leo has a medical degree.' State the contrapositive.
problems.ground_truth: If Leo does not have a medical degree, then Leo is not a doctor.

problems.text: 'If it is a mammal, it is warm-blooded.' What is the contrapositive?
problems.ground_truth: If it is not warm-blooded, then it is not a mammal.

problems.text: 'If the door is open, anyone can enter.' State the contrapositive.
problems.ground_truth: If no one can enter, then the door is not open.

problems.text: 'If she is running, her heart rate is elevated.' What is the contrapositive?
problems.ground_truth: If her heart rate is not elevated, then she is not running.

problems.text: 'If the program is correct, it produces no errors.' State the contrapositive.
problems.ground_truth: If the program produces errors, then it is not correct.

problems.text: 'If you are in Paris, you are in France.' What is the contrapositive?
problems.ground_truth: If you are not in France, then you are not in Paris.

problems.text: 'If Kai passes all courses, Kai graduates.' State the contrapositive.
problems.ground_truth: If Kai does not graduate, then Kai did not pass all courses.

problems.text: It is NOT the case that both Alice and Bob passed. What is an equivalent statement?
problems.ground_truth: Alice did not pass, or Bob did not pass (or both).

problems.text: It is false that the car is fast AND fuel-efficient. Restate using De Morgan's Law.
problems.ground_truth: The car is not fast, or it is not fuel-efficient (or both).

problems.text: It is not true that both the printer and scanner work. What follows by De Morgan's Law?
problems.ground_truth: The printer does not work, or the scanner does not work (or both).

problems.text: 'Not (P and Q)' is equivalent to what?
It is not the case that Sam is tall and strong. What can you conclude?
problems.ground_truth: Sam is not tall, or Sam is not strong (or both).

problems.text: The statement 'it is false that both conditions A and B hold' is equivalent to what?
problems.ground_truth: Condition A does not hold, or condition B does not hold (or both).

problems.text: Not (the sky is blue AND the grass is green). Rewrite this.
problems.ground_truth: The sky is not blue, or the grass is not green (or both).

problems.text: It is not the case that the test is easy and short. What follows?
problems.ground_truth: The test is not easy, or the test is not short (or both).

problems.text: 'Not (raining and cold)' — rewrite using De Morgan's Law.
problems.ground_truth: It is not raining, or it is not cold (or both).

problems.text: It is false that both X and Y are positive. What can you conclude?
problems.ground_truth: X is not positive, or Y is not positive (or both).

problems.text: Not (the restaurant is cheap AND good). What does this mean?
problems.ground_truth: The restaurant is not cheap, or not good (or both).

problems.text: It is not the case that Mia is a singer and a dancer. What follows?
problems.ground_truth: Mia is not a singer, or Mia is not a dancer (or both).

problems.text: Not (the software is fast AND reliable). Restate.
problems.ground_truth: The software is not fast, or not reliable (or both).

problems.text: It is false that both Leo and Zoe were invited. What can you conclude?
problems.ground_truth: Leo was not invited, or Zoe was not invited (or both).

problems.text: Not (it is Monday AND sunny). Rewrite.
problems.ground_truth: It is not Monday, or it is not sunny (or both).

problems.text: It is not the case that the answer is correct and complete. What follows?
problems.ground_truth: The answer is not correct, or not complete (or both).

problems.text: Not (the room is clean AND quiet). What does this mean?
problems.ground_truth: The room is not clean, or not quiet (or both).

problems.text: It is false that both flights are on time. What can you conclude?
problems.ground_truth: The first flight is not on time, or the second is not on time (or both).

problems.text: Not (A ∧ B) where A='the cat is black' and B='the cat is large'. Restate.
problems.ground_truth: The cat is not black, or the cat is not large (or both).

problems.text: It is not the case that Quinn passed math and science. What follows?
problems.ground_truth: Quinn did not pass math, or Quinn did not pass science (or both).

problems.ground_truth: Alice did not pass AND Bob did not pass.

problems.text: It is not true that either the left or right path leads home. What follows?

problems.text: Not (Mia or Leo attended the party). What can you conclude?

problems.text: It is false that it is hot or humid. Restate.
problems.ground_truth: It is not hot AND it is not humid.

problems.text: It is false that either candidate won a majority. What can you conclude?
problems.ground_truth: The first candidate did not win a majority AND the second candidate did not win a majority.

problems.text: Not (the experiment succeeded or was repeated). What follows?
problems.ground_truth: The experiment did not succeed AND was not repeated.

Math is harder than English. English is harder than Art. Compare Math and Art.

problems.ground_truth: The oak tree is older than the birch.

Paris is farther from Tokyo than London is. London is farther from Tokyo than Berlin is. Compare Paris and Berlin in distance from Tokyo.
problems.ground_truth: Paris is farther from Tokyo than Berlin.

Gold is denser than silver. Silver is denser than aluminum. Compare gold and aluminum.
Task A takes longer than Task B. Task B takes longer than Task C. Which task takes longest?
Novel X has more pages than Novel Y. Novel Y has more pages than Novel Z. Compare X and Z.
problems.ground_truth: Novel X has more pages than Novel Z.

problems.ground_truth: The CEO ranks above the manager.

problems.text: River A is longer than River B. River B is longer than River C. Which river is longest?
Diamond is harder than quartz. Quartz is harder than talc. Compare diamond and talc.
Alice scored higher than Bob. Bob scored higher than Carol. Who scored highest?
If speed(A) > speed(B) and speed(B) > speed(C), what can you say about speed(A) vs speed(C)?
Assume there is a largest prime number N. Then consider N! + 1. It is not divisible by any number ≤ N, contradicting that N is the largest prime. What can you conclude?
problems.ground_truth: There is no largest prime number; there are infinitely many primes.

problems.text: Assume √2 is rational, i.e., √2 = p/q in lowest terms. Then 2q² = p², so p is even. Then p = 2k, giving 2q² = 4k², so q is even. But p and q cannot both be even if p/q is in lowest terms. What follows?
Assume that the sum of two odd numbers is odd. Let them be 2a+1 and 2b+1. Their sum is 2(a+b+1), which is even — a contradiction. What can you conclude?
problems.ground_truth: The sum of two odd numbers is even.

problems.text: Assume a triangle has two right angles. Then the sum of angles exceeds 180°, which contradicts the triangle angle sum theorem. What follows?
problems.ground_truth: A triangle cannot have two right angles.

problems.text: Assume there exists an integer that is both even and odd. Then it is divisible by 2 and leaves remainder 1 when divided by 2 — a contradiction. What can you conclude?
problems.ground_truth: No integer is both even and odd.

problems.text: Assume the empty set is not a subset of every set. Then there exists an element in the empty set not in some set S. But the empty set has no elements — contradiction. What follows?
problems.ground_truth: The empty set is a subset of every set.

problems.text: Assume that log₂(3) is rational, equal to a/b. Then 2^(a/b) = 3, so 2^a = 3^b. But a power of 2 cannot equal a power of 3 (unique prime factorization). What can you conclude?
Assume statement S and its negation ¬S are both true. This is a direct contradiction. What follows in classical logic?
problems.ground_truth: The assumption is false; S and ¬S cannot both be true.

problems.text: Assume a chess board missing two diagonally opposite corners can be tiled by dominoes. Each domino covers one black and one white square. The removed squares are the same color, leaving unequal counts — contradiction. What follows?
problems.ground_truth: The board cannot be tiled by dominoes.

problems.text: Assume that among any 3 people, it is possible that none of them know each other and none are mutual strangers. By the Pigeonhole Principle applied to 2 relationship types, at least 2 of the 3 must share a type — contradiction. What can you conclude?
problems.ground_truth: Among any 3 people, either at least 2 know each other or at least 2 are mutual strangers.

problems.text: Assume line L is both parallel and not parallel to line M. This is a contradiction. What follows?
problems.ground_truth: The assumption is false; a line cannot be both parallel and not parallel to another line.

problems.text: Assume 0.999... ≠ 1. Let d = 1 - 0.999... > 0. But no positive number d can be found between them (since 10d = 10 - 9.999... = d). Contradiction. What can you conclude?
Assume a function is continuous on [a,b], f(a) < 0 < f(b), but f has no root in (a,b). By the Intermediate Value Theorem, f must cross zero — contradiction. What follows?
problems.ground_truth: The function has at least one root in (a,b).

problems.text: Assume an even number greater than 2 is prime. Then it is divisible by 2 and thus not prime — contradiction. What can you conclude?
problems.ground_truth: No even number greater than 2 is prime.

problems.text: Assume there is a set of all sets. It would contain itself. Consider the subset of sets that don't contain themselves — this leads to Russell's Paradox. What follows?
problems.ground_truth: There is no set of all sets.

problems.text: Assume two distinct lines in a plane intersect at two different points. Two points determine a unique line — contradiction. What can you conclude?
problems.ground_truth: Two distinct lines can intersect at most at one point.

problems.text: Assume a non-zero number x satisfies x = -x. Then 2x = 0, so x = 0, contradicting x ≠ 0. What follows?
problems.ground_truth: No non-zero number equals its own negation.

problems.text: Assume the set of real numbers between 0 and 1 is countable. Cantor's diagonal argument constructs a real number not in the list — contradiction. What can you conclude?
problems.ground_truth: The set of real numbers between 0 and 1 is uncountable.

problems.text: Assume n² is even but n is odd. Then n = 2k+1 and n² = 4k²+4k+1, which is odd — contradicting n² being even. What follows?
problems.ground_truth: If n² is even, then n is even.

problems.text: Assume a finite group has no identity element. Group axioms require an identity — contradiction. What can you conclude?
problems.ground_truth: Every finite group has an identity element.

problems.text: All mammals are warm-blooded. A dog is a mammal. What can you conclude about the dog?

problems.text: All metals conduct electricity. Copper is a metal. What can you conclude?

problems.text: All roses are flowers. This rose is a rose. What can you conclude?

All squares are rectangles. Figure S is a square. What can you conclude?

All fruits contain seeds. An apple is a fruit. What can you conclude?

Every function in this module is tested. parse() is in this module. What follows?

'You pass if and only if you score above 60.' You scored 75. What follows?
'The door opens if and only if the key is correct.' The door opened. What can you conclude?
'A number is even if and only if it is divisible by 2.' The number is not divisible by 2. What follows?
'It is Tuesday if and only if the store has a sale.' It is not Tuesday. What can you conclude?
problems.ground_truth: The store does not have a sale.

problems.text: 'X = Y if and only if Y = X.' X equals Y. What follows?
'The alarm rings if and only if there is an intruder.' There is no intruder. What can you conclude?
'A figure is a square if and only if it is a rectangle with equal sides.' The figure is a rectangle with equal sides. What follows?
'It rains if and only if clouds are present.' It is not raining. What can you conclude?

problems.ground_truth: P implies Q, and Q implies P.

problems.text: 'Alice attends if and only if Bob attends.' Alice is attending. What can you conclude?
'The circuit is complete if and only if current flows.' Current is not flowing. What follows?
'Leo is eligible if and only if Leo is 18 or older.' Leo is 17. What can you conclude?
'It is daytime if and only if the sun is up.' The sun is up. What follows?
'The function returns true if and only if the input is valid.' The function returned false. What can you conclude?

'A reaction occurs if and only if the catalyst is present.' No reaction occurred. What can you conclude?

If I study, I pass. If I work, I earn money. I will either study or work. What can you conclude?

problems.text: If it rains, we use an umbrella. If it snows, we wear a coat. It will either rain or snow. What follows?
problems.ground_truth: We will either use an umbrella or wear a coat.

problems.text: If Alice applies, she gets an interview. If Bob applies, he gets an interview. Either Alice or Bob will apply. What can you conclude?
